report:
**Conclusion:** Clinical evidence supports the claim. Preoperative skin preparation with chlorhexidine-alcohol significantly reduces the risk of surgical-site infections (SSIs) compared with iodine-alcohol or povidone-iodine preparations.

### Key Evidence
* **Randomized Trial Evidence:** A landmark study published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* demonstrated that chlorhexidine–alcohol skin antisepsis before cesarean delivery resulted in a significantly lower risk of superficial or deep SSIs within 30 days compared with iodine–alcohol (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1511048).
* **Cochrane Review:** A systematic evaluation concluded with moderate certainty that skin preparation with chlorhexidine gluconate prior to cesarean section is more effective at preventing SSIs than povidone–iodine (https://www.cochrane.org/CD007462/PREG_skin-preparation-preventing-infection-following-caesarean-section).
* **Network Meta-Analysis:** A network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found that alcohol-based 2% chlorhexidine had the highest probability of preventing SSIs after cesarean delivery, outperforming alcohol-based povidone–iodine (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195670124001282).
* **Systematic Meta-Analysis:** A meta-analysis focusing on randomized trials comparing chlorhexidine-alcohol with povidone-iodine for cesarean delivery confirmed superior reduction of surgical-site infections with chlorhexidine-alcohol (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30184558/).
